Call `set_attributes()` on that turn's span object while the turn is open. Because you're instrumenting the agent by hand, this is the Agents data-model approach, not the legacy `weave.attributes` context manager for Calls.

```python
import weave

weave.init("[TEAM-NAME]/[PROJECT-NAME]")

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent"):
    with weave.start_turn(user_message="What is the weather in Tokyo?") as turn:
        turn.set_attributes({"env": "staging"})
```

This pattern follows the docs' example of stamping attributes on a turn span. That example uses `user_id`, `tenant` and `env` [S1]. `set_attributes()` stamps arbitrary attributes on a single span. You can pass a dictionary with one key or many, and the method returns the span, so you can chain calls [S1].

**Things to know**
- **Timing:** Set the attributes after the span starts and before it ends, which in Python means inside the `with` block. On a span that hasn't started or has already ended, the call is a no-op and logs a warning [S3].
- **Key names:** `env` is a custom key, so Weave stores it as a filterable custom attribute. Avoid keys under the reserved `weave.*` and `gen_ai.*` prefixes [S1]. The docs say a custom value under a reserved key is unsupported [S2].
- **Scope:** Other spans in the conversation don't get the attribute. The same method is available on `LLM`, `Tool` and `SubAgent` spans, for example `tool.set_attributes(...)` [S1]. If you wanted `env` on every span in the conversation, pass `attributes={...}` to `weave.start_conversation(...)` [S2].
- **Batch logging:** If you log completed activity in a batch with `log_turn` or `log_conversation`, populate the span object's declared fields and pass the object in. The docs point to a separate batch guide for this [S3]. I didn't read that guide.

I haven't run this example, because the Weave SDK isn't available in my offline sandbox. It's based on the documentation examples above.

# Set attributes and events on agent spans

> Attach custom attributes and record events on agent spans (Turn, LLM, Tool, and SubAgent) to filter and analyze agent activity in Weave.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/attributes-and-events).

When you instrument an agent with the Weave SDK, each span object (`Turn`, `LLM`, `Tool`, and `SubAgent`) exposes methods to attach custom metadata. Use these methods to stamp contextual information such as user IDs, tenants, experiment names, or environment labels onto agent spans, then filter and group agent activity by that metadata in the Weights & Biases UI.

This metadata comes in two forms:

* **Attributes**: Key-value properties of a span as a whole. Use `set_attributes()` (Python) or `setAttributes()` (TypeScript) to stamp attributes on a single span, or set conversation-wide attributes that apply to every span a conversation emits.
* **Events**: Point-in-time markers that occur during a span's lifetime, such as a permission prompt or a lifecycle transition. Use `add_event()` (Python) or `addEvent()` (TypeScript).

These methods mirror the [OpenTelemetry (OTel) span API](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-spans/): `set_attributes` mirrors OTel's `Span.set_attributes`, and `add_event` mirrors OTel's `Span.add_event`. The Weave SDK emits OTel spans and stores all attributes, so they remain queryable in Weave.

sources.heading: When you can set attributes
sources.text:
## When you can set attributes

Set attributes while the span is recording, that is, after the span starts and before it ends. In Python, this is inside the `with` block. In TypeScript, this is after `start*()` and before `end()`.

If you call `set_attributes()`, or its TypeScript equivalent on a span that hasn't started yet or has already ended, the call is a no-op and logs a warning that names the fix.

The call is silent (no warning) only when OTel isn't installed or Weave is disabled.

> [!TIP]
>
> To attach attributes when logging completed agent activity in a single batch rather than during live execution, populate the span object's declared fields directly and pass the object to `log_turn` or `log_conversation`. See [Log agent activity in batches](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents-batch.md).

# Turn

> TypeScript SDK reference

[GitHub source](https://github.com/wandb/weave/blob/7c9efdc9fe05ffcaf2430dd652ef9bc5b3ffdfaa/sdks/node/src/genai/turn.ts#L98)

An agent invocation. Typically wraps the work to respond to a single
user message. Emits an `invoke_agent` span and acts as the root of the
trace for that turn: it is always started under `ROOT_CONTEXT` so it
never accidentally inherits a parent from another OTel-instrumented
library.

Created by `weave.startTurn()` (or `conversation.startTurn()`) and
terminated with `end()`. Only one Turn may be active in an async chain.
Children (LLM, Tool, SubAgent) attach via the `startLLM`, `startTool`,
`startSubagent` methods.

results.title: Send OpenTelemetry Traces to Weave
results.heading: Attribute mappings
results.snippet:
## Attribute mappings

Weave maps OpenTelemetry span attributes from various instrumentation frameworks to its internal data model. This mapping means you don't need to rename or transform attributes from your existing instrumentation to get a rich view in Weave. When multiple attribute names map to the same field, Weave applies them in priority order, which lets frameworks coexist in the same traces.

results.title: weave
results.heading: <kbd>method</kbd> `record`
results.snippet:
### <kbd>method</kbd> `record`

```python theme={"system"}
record(
    messages: 'list[Message] | None' = None,
    system_instructions: 'list[str] | None' = None,
    agent_name: 'str | None' = None,
    model: 'str | None' = None,
    agent_id: 'str | None' = None,
    agent_description: 'str | None' = None,
    agent_version: 'str | None' = None
) → Turn
```

Set multiple turn fields in one call.

Collapses the per-field assignments a manually-instrumented agent otherwise makes on a turn (`system_instructions`, `agent_id`, ...) into a single keyword call. Only fields explicitly passed (non-`None`) are applied — existing values are preserved. `messages` **replaces** the turn's existing messages (unlike `Turn.user(...)`, which appends a single message). Returns `self` for chaining. Mirrors `LLM.record`.

Note: on the streaming (`with`) path the turn span is named from `agent_name` at `__enter__`, so set `agent_name` via `start_turn` rather than `record` if you need the span name to reflect it; `record` still updates the `gen_ai.agent.name` attribute.

# track metadata alongside the previously defined function
